caption: WikiText validation perplexity of LLaMA1-7B, LLaMA1-13B and Vicuna-7B pruned by various M at 70% sparsity using OWL.
annotation: The line plot illustrate the perplexity of three different models, LLAMA1-7B, LLAMA1-13B, and Vicuna-7B, against a parameter M on validation set of WikiText dataset. The x-axis represents parameter M, with a linear scale with values ranging from 3 to 8 at an interval of 1. The y-axis denotes perplexity, also on a linear scale, ranging from 20.0 to 40.0, with tick labels at intervals of 10. The green line, representing LLAMA1-7B, utilizes circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at M=3, with a perplexity of approximately 28.0 and then at M=5, it has minimum perplexity of 25.0, and then it increases to about 35.0 at M=8. The orange line for LLAMA1-13B features star-shaped markers with a solid line. It starts at approximately 20.0 at M=3, reaches its minimum at M=6, and then returns to around 19.0 at M=8. The blue line with triangular markers, indicative of Vicuna-7B. It begins at a perplexity of about 41.0 at M=3, trends downward to reach a minimum of approximately 34.0 at M=7, and rises back to around 39.0 at M=8. A legend is also provided at the centre right of plot which map the different colors of line to their LLM architecture names.
paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models

caption: We compare error rate (one minus accuracy), computation cost, and memory usage across our approach and baselines when fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks. MTL-FT refers to first fine-tuning a shared LoRA on all the datasets, and then fine-tuning the low-rank adapter on each dataset, while Full FT refers to full fine-tuning of the entire model. Our approach boosts the test accuracy of QLoRA by 10\% on average, only incurring 8\% additional computation and 9 GB more memory. It performs on par with the best baseline with 45\% less FLOPs.

Each year features stacked bars that represent datasets for various languages. The colors of the bars correspond to different languages as indicated by the legend: blue for English, orange for "All other" languages, green for Arabic, red for Bengali, purple for Spanish, and brown for Russian. From 2012 to 2015, only "English" had at least one dataset. In 2016, "English" had 10 datasets, and "All Other" had datasets ranging from 1 to 10. In 2017, for example, the tallest segment is for English, followed by "All other" languages, both of which reach between 10^1 and 10^2.
